name: Manual
caption: When manually started

configuration.description: Optional table number the flow runs on. 0 (or absent) = standalone flow without a record. When set, every start needs exactly one record of this table, which becomes the Rec output.

When the execution card opens after a run a user started and waited for: 0 = Never (a failed run is offered), 1 = On error, 2 = Always. Unknown values are treated as 0. Runs without a waiting user (from other flows, silent, background) never open it.

Array of page numbers (integers) on which the flow is offered through the "Start Flow" page action. Only pages that carry that action are allowed (see notes). 0 and duplicates are ignored. For a record-based flow each page must show records of tableNo.

outputs.name: Rec
outputs.when: only when configuration.tableNo is non-zero; tableNo = configuration.tableNo

rules.check: If configuration.tableNo is non-zero, the table must exist in the environment. Hard stop at publish (trigger validation). The editor's status line does not check it.
rules.message: The table %1 the flow runs on does not exist.

rules.check: Every page in configuration.pages must be one of the pages that carry the "Start Flow" action. Hard stop at publish; the config canvas status line shows it live and the page picker only offers these pages.
rules.message: The page %1 cannot show the "Start Flow" action.

rules.check: For a record-based flow (tableNo <> 0), every assigned page must show records of that table. Standalone flows (tableNo = 0) fit every supported page. Hard stop at publish; also shown live in the config canvas status line.
rules.message: The page %1 shows records of the table %2, but the flow runs on the table %3.

rules.check: The flow header must have a Code (not part of the definition JSON). Checked before the licensing call.
rules.message: Enter a Code on the flow card before publishing this flow. Manual flows are started from other flows and from extensions by their Code.

rules.check: configuration.openExecution should be 0, 1 or 2. Not checked; any other value behaves like 0 (Never).
Starting the flow (API, Start flow step, page action) requires a published version.
rules.message: The flow %1 is not active. Publish it before starting it.

rules.check: Only flows whose published trigger is Manual can be started by Code.
rules.message: The flow %1 cannot be started this way, because it is not started by the trigger "When manually started".

rules.check: A record-based flow must be started with a record.
rules.message: The flow %1 runs on a record of the table %2. Pass a record to start it.

rules.check: A standalone flow must be started without a record.
rules.message: The flow %1 does not run on a record. Start it without one.

rules.check: The record passed must be of configuration.tableNo.
rules.message: The flow %1 runs on records of the table %2, not of the table %3.

rules.check: Started from a card page, the record must already be saved.
rules.message: Save the record before starting a flow on it.

notes: Execution is asynchronous: each start creates one pending execution (one per record for a record-based flow) plus its own Job Queue entry, queued in the caller's transaction. Interactive starts (flow card, Flow Workspace, page action) then commit and follow the run in a wait dialog. No recurring Job Queue entry is created on publish.

Integration callers choose a run mode: WaitDialog, Silent, FireAndForget (default for the external contract; queues in the caller's transaction, nothing is committed) or Inline (commits, then runs the flow to its end in the caller's session without the Job Queue; a step that defers itself, e.g. Sleep, fails the flow in this mode with 'The flow stopped before its end and cannot continue when it runs in this session.').
Asynchronous runs commit after every step (no trigger in AutoFlow currently opts into one-transaction runs).

Starting a record-based flow from the flow card shows a filter page on the table and starts one execution per matching record (confirmation when more than one; message 'No records match the filters, so the flow was not started.' when none).

Pages that carry the "Start Flow" action (card + list of each): Sales Quote 41 / Sales Quotes 9300, Sales Order 42 / Sales Order List 9305, Sales Invoice 43 / Sales Invoice List 9301, Sales Credit Memo 44 / Sales Credit Memos 9302, Sales Return Order 6630 / Sales Return Order List 9304, Blanket Sales Order 507 / Blanket Sales Orders 9303, Posted Sales Invoice 132 / Posted Sales Invoices 143, Posted Sales Credit Memo 134 / Posted Sales Credit Memos 144, Posted Sales Shipment 130 / Posted Sales Shipments 142, Purchase Quote 49 / Purchase Quotes 9306, Purchase Order 50 / Purchase Order List 9307, Purchase Invoice 51 / Purchase Invoices 9308, Purchase Credit Memo 52 / Purchase Credit Memos 9309, Purchase Return Order 6640 / Purchase Return Order List 9311, Blanket Purchase Order 509 / Blanket Purchase Orders 9310, Posted Purchase Invoice 138 / Posted Purchase Invoices 146, Posted Purchase Credit Memo 140 / Posted Purchase Credit Memos 147, Posted Purchase Receipt 136 / Posted Purchase Receipts 145, Reminder 434 / Reminder List 436, Issued Reminder 438 / Issued Reminder List 440, Customer Card 21 / Customer List 22, Vendor Card 26 / Vendor List 27, Item Card 30 / Item List 31, Contact Card 5050 / Contact List 5052. Page numbers are the standard Business Central ones; extensions may register additional pages. The validator in this repo cannot know extension-registered pages.
Page assignments take effect on publish. A page shows the action only while an active (published, Manual-trigger) flow is assigned to it and the flow's table fits the page.
The Step Selector offers each published Manual flow as its own tile (via the Start flow step); the generic Start flow action itself is hidden from the picker.

Picker filters that depend on the trigger: Respond to Webhook, Return SubFlow Output, Return PDF, Set report file name, Set document field values and Prevent page close are hidden in a Manual flow (they only apply to their own triggers).
The trigger step slug is always 'trigger', so the record is referenced as {{trigger_Rec}}.
